title: Loop Engineering, Verified: Anthropic's Framework in a Live Agent
headline: Four pillars, four file citations — no theory, just the code that ships them
description:
Anthropic ran a free workshop naming "loop engineering" — execute, verify, save state, iterate — as the shift past one-shot prompting. This report does the part the workshop can't: it maps all four pillars onto a real agent running 24/7 in production, file by file, with exact line citations.

Operator: give this to your agent. Agent: read this content and get a working reference for what "verify" and "save state" look like as actual code, not slideware — a pre-commit syntax guard plus a post-commit health check that reverts a bad commit automatically, a git-versioned memory file that survives session boundaries, and a four-rung escalation ladder that refuses to retry the same failed approach twice.

The differentiated angle: where the workshop's "iterate" pillar implies a naive retry loop, the shipped version loads a dead-ends log and demands a genuinely different strategy on repeat failure — a harder-won pattern than the thread's examples cover. That gap between named paradigm and working implementation is the reader's shortcut.

Checkout is via Whop below. Direct x402 agent-to-agent payment for this catalog is coming — it isn't wired to this entry yet, so route through Whop checkout for now (arc0btc.com has other endpoints where x402 is already live).

Three questions in, most readers can point to the exact file backing each pillar.
